title: Closed-point purity descends from the strict completion
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, ordinary small-etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], finite Tate twists [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist], and the canonical Kummer class of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus], with the bounded-below closed-support adjunction [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction].

Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] with $\ell$ invertible and $d=\dim R$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Fix a separable closure $k^{\mathrm{sep}}$ of its residue field $k$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Let $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ be the strict henselization at this geometric closed point [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and let $B=\widehat{R^{\mathrm{sh}}}$ be its maximal-ideal completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. The ring $B$ is Noetherian regular local, complete strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], of dimension $d$, with residue field $k^{\mathrm{sep}}$ and with $\ell$ invertible. Write $j_R:\operatorname{Spec}k\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $j_B:\operatorname{Spec}k^{\mathrm{sep}}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}B$ for the closed immersions [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-closed-immersion]. If the canonical Kummer map $A_{k^{\mathrm{sep}}}\to j_B^!A_B(d)[2d]$ is an isomorphism, then $A_k\to j_R^!A_R(d)[2d]$ is an isomorphism. No excellence hypothesis on $R$ is assumed.

source.place: Expose XVI, paragraph after Definition 3.2.1 and Proposition 3.2.4, printed p.244: strict henselization invariance and completion invariance. The one-way closed-point formulation is a new statement-only obligation, without the withdrawn ind-etale proof graph.

proof.text: The item's ring $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is the affine pointed-neighbourhood colimit at the geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ induced by $R\to k\subset k^{\mathrm{sep}}\subset\Omega$, $\Omega$ an algebraic closure of $k^{\mathrm{sep}}$. The geometric-triples colimit comparison, applied to the triples colimit below (a henselian local ind-etale $R$-algebra with residue surjection onto $k^{\mathrm{sep}}$ extending $R\to k$), gives a unique $R$-algebra isomorphism of this colimit with $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ compatible with the residue maps; we identify them. Put $C=R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and $K=k^{\mathrm{sep}}$. The strict-henselization triples theorem gives a filtered-colimit presentation of $C$ by etale $R$-algebras, strict henselianity, maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mC$ and the specified identification $C/\mathfrak n=K$. The three cited strict-henselization lemmas give, respectively, Noetherianity, regularity and $\dim C=d$. In particular $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is an affine ind-etale morphism between Noetherian schemes, and its Cartesian inverse image of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is exactly $\operatorname{Spec}K$. The inverse of $\ell$ in $R$ maps to an inverse in $C$.

For $B=\widehat C$, the strict-henselization-completion lemma gives Noetherianity and faithful flatness of $C\to B$. Completion regularity and dimension give regularity and $\dim B=d$. The local-completion lemma identifies the maximal ideal with $\mathfrak nB$ and the residue field with $C/\mathfrak n=K$, compatibly with the completion map. Since $\mathfrak n$ is finitely generated, the module-completion theorem, applied to the $C$-module $C$, makes $B$ complete and separated for $(\mathfrak nB)^r=\mathfrak n^rB$. Complete-pair henselianity now makes $(B,\mathfrak nB)$ henselian; its separably closed residue field makes $B$ strictly henselian. Also $\ell$ is invertible in $B$. These establish every ring-property clause of the statement without an excellence hypothesis.

Choose $d$ generators $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ of $\mathfrak m$, as allowed by the definition of regular local ring. Their images generate $\mathfrak n$ and $\mathfrak nB$ by Steps 1--2. The regular-local-generators lemma applied separately to $R,C,B$ makes these three lists regular sequences and their successive quotients regular local of dimensions $d-c$. Thus the three closed-point immersions are regular closed immersions of codimension $d$. The strict-henselization map is faithfully flat by the cited lemma, and the completion map is faithfully flat by Step 2, so class-calculus flat base change applies to both pairs. In particular their canonical Kummer classes, with the given sign and ordering independence, are the pullbacks of the class defined using the $t_i$. If $d=0$, each list is empty and the same class-calculus statement gives the identity class.

proof.text: Write $j_C:\operatorname{Spec}K\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}C$, $g:\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, and $h:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Apply affine ind-etale support exchange to the Cartesian closed-point square of Step 1 and $A_R(d)[2d]$. Tate pullback identifies its target with $j_C^!A_C(d)[2d]$, giving $h^*j_R^!A_R(d)[2d]\simeq j_C^!A_C(d)[2d]$. Under this canonical counit-normalized exchange, $h^*\eta_R$ is $\eta_C$: class calculus gives strict-local compatibility of the supported class, and transposing its supported map through the fixed closed adjunction gives the asserted equality of morphisms. Hence it suffices to prove $\eta_C$ is an isomorphism. Indeed, if so, $h^*\eta_R$ is one; every geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ factors through $h$, since the separable algebraic extension $K/k$ embeds over $k$ into the algebraically closed field $\Omega'$; pullback-stalk comparison then shows that $\eta_R$ is an isomorphism on every geometric stalk of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, and derived stalk conservativity proves the claim. One may use an algebraic closure $\Omega$ containing $K$ as the geometric point; extending the chosen separable closure to such a field does not change $C$.

proof.text: Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $\widehat X=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $f:\widehat X\to X$, and $F=A_X(d)$ in degree zero. Tate pullback identifies $f^{-1}F$ with $A_{\widehat X}(d)$. Since $C$ and $B$ are strictly henselian, their higher etale cohomology of these sheaves vanishes. For degree zero, choose the same geometric closed point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, with $K\subseteq\Omega$ algebraically closed, on both schemes. The sections-stalk isomorphisms and inverse-image stalk comparison identify the section pullback with the identity of the stalk $F_{\bar s}$. Thus the canonical maps $H^q(X,F)\to H^q(\widehat X,f^{-1}F)$ are isomorphisms for all $q$: the above handles $q\geq0$, and negative groups vanish since $F$ is in degree zero. All identifications respect the $A$-actions.

source.place: Tag 03QO (lemma-vanishing-etale-cohomology-strictly-henselian), Tag 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback); Tate pullback via Tag 03PK (section-kummer).

proof.text: Let $s=V(\mathfrak n)$ in $X$, $\widehat s=V(\mathfrak nB)$ in $\widehat X$, $U=X\setminus\{s\}$ and $\widehat U=\widehat X\setminus\{\widehat s\}$. By Step 2 these closed subschemes are both $\operatorname{Spec}K$ and form a Cartesian square; $\widehat U=f^{-1}U$. Apply the no-excellence henselian-completion open-rigidity statement with the Noetherian ring $C$, ideal $\mathfrak n$ and torsion abelian sheaf $F|_U$. Its henselian-pair hypothesis follows from Step 1; its completion is the specified $B$. The sheaf is killed by $\ell$, so it is torsion. It gives the canonical isomorphisms $H^q(U,F|_U)\simeq H^q(\widehat U,f^{-1}F|_{\widehat U})$ for every $q\geq0$. Negative cohomology again vanishes. This comparison applies equally when the puncture is empty.

source.place: Expose XX, section 4.4, printed p.373, CTC and its strictly local displayed assertion (*).

proof.text: Apply the localization long exact sequence to $(X,s,F)$ and $(\widehat X,\widehat s,f^{-1}F)$. Its functoriality in the pair and the sheaf gives a commutative diagram with the canonical pullbacks on whole-space, open and supported groups, including the connecting maps. For every integer $q$, take the five consecutive terms $H^{q-1}(X,F)$, $H^{q-1}(U,F)$, $H_s^q(X,F)$, $H^q(X,F)$, $H^q(U,F)$ and the corresponding bottom row. The four outer vertical maps are isomorphisms by Steps 5--6; the five lemma gives an isomorphism on the middle supported group. Thus the canonical supported pullback $\beta:R\Gamma_s(X,F)\to R\Gamma_{\widehat s}(\widehat X,f^{-1}F)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, since it induces isomorphisms in every degree. Here $R\Gamma_s$ is the right-derived kernel of restriction, not an independently chosen complex with the same cohomology dimensions.

source.place: Tag 09XP (section-cohomology-support), localization triangle and long exact sequence; Homology Tag 05QB (lemma-five-lemma).

proof.text: For $T=X,\widehat X$, with closed immersion $i:\operatorname{Spec}K\hookrightarrow T$, the supported-kernel adjunction identifies the supported subsheaf of any sheaf $M$ with $i_*i_0^!M$. This identity respects $A$-actions by its naturality with respect to multiplication by each $a\in A$. Evaluate on a bounded-below injective module resolution $I$ of the coefficient sheaf. The definition of the closed-support adjoint and injective computation of right derived functors identify $i_0^!I$ with $i^!F_T$. Since $K$ is separably closed, it is strictly henselian as a local ring. Its global-sections functor is exact. Consequently both $R\Gamma(K,i^!F_T)$ and $R\Gamma_i(T,F_T)$ are represented by the same complex $\Gamma(K,i_0^!I)=\ker(I(T)\to I(T\setminus i(K)))$. These are the canonical support/counit identifications. This module complex also computes the abelian groups $H^p_{i(K)}(T,F_T)$ of Step 7: each $I^q$ is killed by $\ell$, its underlying abelian sheaf has vanishing higher cohomology on every etale $T$-scheme by the injective-module acyclicity lemma, and $I^q(T)\to I^q(T\setminus i(K))$ is surjective by the injective restriction lemma, so the support sequence gives $H^p_{i(K)}(T,I^q)=0$ for $p\geq1$. Furthermore $R\Gamma(K,-)$ detects isomorphisms on $D^+$: exactness computes its cohomology by applying sections to cohomology sheaves, sections-stalk identifies those groups with every geometric stalk on $\operatorname{Spec}K$, and derived stalk conservativity applies.

proof.text: Under Step 8 the maps $R\Gamma(K,\eta_C)$ and $R\Gamma(K,\eta_B)$ have source $A[0]$ and targets $R\Gamma_s(X,A(d))[2d]$ and $R\Gamma_{\widehat s}(\widehat X,A(d))[2d]$. Flat compatibility of the Kummer supported class (Step 3) says that the first followed by $\beta[2d]$ is the second. This is equality of derived morphisms: a map from $A[0]$ to a complex of $A$-modules is determined by the cohomology class of the image of $1$, and these images are exactly the canonical fundamental classes that flat pullback identifies. The second map is an isomorphism by the hypothesis on $\eta_B$; $\beta[2d]$ is an isomorphism by Step 7. Hence $R\Gamma(K,\eta_C)$ is an isomorphism, and the conservativity in Step 8 makes $\eta_C$ an isomorphism. Step 4 descends this to $\eta_R$. This proves the required implication for the specified canonical map.
